item.title: Core Keeper Base Building Guide — Room Rules, NPC Housing and Automation
item.description: A good Core Keeper base is more than a pile of chests. This base building guide covers the room system, NPC move-in rules, bed mechanics and the automation basics that keep your underground hub running while you explore. Room rules that actually matter Rooms are the core building block of a Core Keeper base. The game recognizes a room when: The enclosed area is between 2×2 and 8×8 tiles (smaller or larger rooms don’t register) It has a door and a bed It contains the required item for the NPC you want (each NPC has a specific item) No players are within 30 tiles of the room for roughly a minute If any condition fails, the room won’t count — and NPCs won’t move in.

item.title: Core Keeper Boss Guide — All 7 Bosses, Drops, Locations and Strategies
item.description: Core Keeper’s boss order follows your tool progression: three bosses around the Core must fall before it powers up, then the outer-ring titans open endgame content. This Core Keeper boss guide lists every boss, where they spawn, how to summon them and what they drop. The three early bosses (power up the Core) Defeat all three and place their drops on the effigies next to the Core to activate it.

item.title: Core Keeper Cooking & Food Buff Guide — Best Recipes and How Buffs Stack
item.description: Food in Core Keeper isn’t just hunger — the right dishes are pre-boss loadouts. This cooking guide explains how food buffs work, which ingredients give the strongest effects, and the best combos before each fight. How food buffs work Food value refills your hunger; hunger loss only reduces max health and stats — you can’t die of starvation. Cooked ingredients give Regen, max health, armor, damage and speed buffs with a duration.

item.title: Core Keeper First Hour Guide — World Creation, Tools and Your First Boss
item.description: The Core Keeper getting started experience is built around one loop: craft a workbench, make stronger tools, mine tougher walls, find better ores, and repeat. This guide walks through world creation, the first hour, and the three early bosses you need to beat before the Core powers up. World creation: what to pick Select Start Game from the main menu to create a world. You can also join a friend’s world from the Steam friends list — Core Keeper has native multiplayer with no dedicated server required, and more than the officially stated 8 players can connect.

item.title: Core Keeper Mods Guide — Where to Download, How to Install and Essential Mods
item.description: Core Keeper supports official modding through Steam Workshop and mod.io, with community content managed by the CoreLib framework. This modding guide covers where to find mods, how to install them, and the most useful quality-of-life mods. Where to get mods Platform What it is Notes Steam Workshop Official in-game mod browser One-click subscribe & install; requires the game mod.io Cross-platform mod repository Browsable online, official Core Keeper page CoreLib Community mod framework / loader Most mods depend on it; install first Check the Mods hub for an indexed list of popular mods and their patch compatibility.

item.title: Core Keeper Ore Tier Guide — Pickaxe Progression and Where Each Ore Spawns
item.description: Core Keeper’s world is generated in rings around the Core, and each ring holds different ores. This Core Keeper ore guide maps every ore to the pickaxe tier and biome you need — so you never waste time mining with the wrong tool. Pickaxe tiers at a glance Pickaxe Workbench Materials Mines Wood Pickaxe Starting inventory Wood Soft dirt walls only Copper Pickaxe Basic Workbench 8 Copper Bar, 10 Wood Copper, Tin Tin Pickaxe Basic Workbench 8 Tin Bar, 10 Wood Iron Iron Pickaxe Iron Anvil 8 Iron Bar, 10 Wood Gold, Scarlet Gold Pickaxe Gold Anvil 8 Gold Bar, 10 Wood Harder ores, faster Scarlet Pickaxe Scarlet Workbench 8 Scarlet Bar, 10 Wood Best pre-endgame speed You can technically mine anywhere from the start — but stronger walls block exploration until your pickaxe tier catches up.

item.title: Core Keeper World Seeds Guide — How Seeds Shape Your World
item.description: Every Core Keeper world is generated from a seed — the number you pick at world creation. The seed decides where each biome ring sits, which direction you find the Clay Caves, and roughly where the early bosses spawn. This guide explains how seed generation works and how to use seeds with friends. What a seed controls Aspect Seed-dependent Biome angles Yes — Clay Caves / Forgotten Ruins each occupy half of the world beyond the chasm; the exact angle varies by seed Outer biome order Yes — the three outer biomes (Azeos’ Wilderness, Sunken Sea, Mold) rotate counter-clockwise per seed Boss placement Partly — Glurch spawns ~65 tiles in a random angle; boss arc segments shift with the seed World shape / ring distances No — the ring band structure (0–140, 150–450, 450–520, 520–1200+) is the same for every world In short: the seed is a rotation and placement key, not a terrain generator.
